patch_description:
The previous implementation failed validation because its recursive value-grouping machinery was fundamentally broken: it relied on `hasattr(row, col)` attribute access on itertuples rows (fails/misses for many column names), wrote rows into `result_df` via `as_completed` (destroying row order and index alignment), manipulated a fabricated "original_index" column with fragile assertions, returned an empty `[]` as column_orderings (violating the required per-row orderings output), and contained assertion paths that crash when grouping/dependency assumptions don't hold (e.g. nunique==1 assertions, shape mismatches after recursive merging, duplicate index asserts).

The fix replaces the whole editable block with a correct, bounded algorithm aligned with the actual objective (character-Trie prefix reuse): build each row's serialization from its cells, generate 3 cheap whole-df candidate constructions (original order, global frequency-weighted column order using sum len(v)*cnt*(cnt-1), and a bounded conditional partition tree), score each with the exact serial-Trie objective (sum of adjacent LCPs of sorted serialized rows, using C-speed slice comparisons), and output the best with valid per-row column orderings. All cell values, rows and shape are preserved exactly (object dtype); col_merge is handled via the parent's merging_columns helper as before.
